metais render — Render the package's outputs from the inputs supplied, into a
new directory.

Usage:
  metais render <package> --out <dir> [supply flags] [--now <time>] [--json]

The package is opened and verified whole, and the inputs are supplied and
validated, as metais inspect and metais validate do; an input that fails ends
the render with every finding of the inputs. Then every output is planned, an
asset or a mirror as each file it writes, its path checked by the portable-path
rules, and rendered in memory: every output is attempted, and each reports its
first error. An asset is copied as it is, never rendered: its size counts
against the output limits, and its bytes are read from the package as it is
written. An output declaring newline: crlf then has its line endings made CR LF,
and one naming a validate schema is parsed and validated against it, every
finding of every output reported. If any finding is an error, nothing is written
anywhere. A container output is one zip of its entries, each rendered as an
output is, in the order its profile and its first entries give; its zip is
written as it is assembled.

--out is required, and names a directory that does not exist yet. The outputs
are written beneath a staging directory beside it, .metais-staging- followed by
16 hex digits, which is then renamed to it in one step that never replaces
anything: the directory either does not exist or holds every output. Its missing
parents are created. An --out that exists is refused before anything is written.

A template sees the inputs as inputs, the package's identity as package, where
each input came from as sources, the output being rendered as output, and the
render time as now, which is --now normalized to UTC, or nil without it. Nothing
of the host — no environment variable, directory, user or clock — reaches a
template.

Each output's path is a Liquid template too. An output with for_each is rendered
once for each element of its array, which its when, its path and its template
see as item, with its position as fan_out; an output, or an element, whose when
is false writes no file.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.

Flags:
  --out <dir>
      The directory to render into, which must not exist; required.
  --data <dir>
      The data directory: one file per input named <input>.<ext>, and one
      directory per collection input. metais inspect lists each input's file
      names.
  --set <pointer>=<text>
      Set one value at an inputs pointer, such as /vendor/name=Acme; the text is
      coerced to the type the schema declares there. Applied after --data and
      --inputs-json, in command-line order with --set-json. May be given more
      than once.
  --set-json <pointer>=<json>
      Set one value at an inputs pointer as JSON text, the way to set null, an
      array or an object. Applied in command-line order with --set. May be given
      more than once.
  --inputs-json <json>
      A JSON object whose members are inputs, each replacing that input's whole
      value; - reads it from standard input, once. Applied after --data, in
      command-line order. May be given more than once.
  --now <date-time>
      The render time, an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, which templates see
      as now; without it there is no time.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  One line per file written, in path order: its size, its digest and its path,
  separated by tabs; a container's entries are indented beneath it, in its
  order. With --json, one metais.render/1 document.

  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais render --help
  usage.bad_value
      --now is not an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset.
      Next: metais render <package> --out <dir> --now 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z
  usage.conflicting_flags
      --inputs-json - is given twice, and standard input is read once.
      Next: metais help inputs
  usage.data_dir_unreadable
      The data directory given to --data does not exist, is not a directory, or
      cannot be read.
      Next: metais render <package> --data <dir> --out <dir>
  usage.missing_flag
      --out is not given.
      Next: metais render <package> --out <dir>
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais render --help
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais render --help

      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais render --help

Examples:
  metais render report-1.0.0.metais --data data --out out
      Renders the package's outputs from the data directory data into the new
      directory out.
  metais render report.metais --data data --set /vendor/name=Acme --out out
      Renders with one value set over the data directory's.
  metais render . --data data --out out --now 2026-10-19T09:30:00+02:00 --json
      Renders the source directory in the working directory with a render time,
      and prints the files as one metais.render/1 document.
